summary: Ran all eight acceptance checks against the built app on http://localhost:3000 — every one passed.
Filtering works from the links and from the URL, an unknown status falls back to All, and the export still downloads the same three sent/paid rows under every filter.
Also tried the awkward cases the spec does not list — empty, repeated, uppercase and misspelled ?status=, a second click, a reload and browser back/forward — all behave as All or hold their filter.

blocks.caption: Check 1: /invoices with no query shows all five seeded invoices, with five links — All, Draft, Sent, Paid, Void — above the table and All in bold.
Check 2: after clicking Draft in the browser, the table holds exactly one row, INV-1004. The other four invoices are gone from the page and Draft is the bold link.
Checks 3 and 5: /invoices?status=paid shows exactly INV-1001 and INV-1003, and Paid is visibly bolder than All, Draft, Sent and Void.
Check 5 measured rather than eyeballed: read from the live DOM, only the Paid anchor carries aria-current="page" and font-weight 700; the other four are 400 with no aria-current.
Check 4: /invoices?status=sent shows exactly one row, INV-1002.
Check 4: /invoices?status=void shows exactly one row, INV-1005.
Check 6: /invoices?status=bogus does not empty the table or error — all five invoices come back and All is the selected link.

blocks.title: What each check exercised

blocks.caption: Check 7: clicking Export while the table showed only the draft downloaded a CSV byte-for-byte identical to the one downloaded with no filter — header plus INV-1001, INV-1002, INV-1003, with INV-1004 and INV-1005 absent. The label stayed "Export 3 invoices as CSV" on every filter.
Beyond the checks: clicking Paid twice, reloading, moving to Void, and going back and forward in browser history each leave exactly one link marked current and the right rows in the table.
Beyond the checks: ?status= empty, repeated (paid&sent), "Paid", "PAID", " paid" and a wrong parameter name all answer 200 and fall back to All rather than erroring or emptying the table.
Check 8: npm run build exits 0 and the route table now lists /invoices as ƒ (Dynamic), the expected consequence of the page reading searchParams.
Check 8: npm test (43 tests in 5 files), npm run typecheck and npm run lint each exit 0.
The browser console across a load and two filter clicks: the only message is the app's pre-existing favicon 404, with no hydration or routing errors from the new links.

focus.title: The export is genuinely untouched by the filter
focus.detail: This is the product rule the app exists to hold, so it was checked by downloading the file twice in a real browser rather than by reading the code: once with the table filtered to Draft and once with no filter. The two files are byte-for-byte identical — header plus INV-1001, INV-1002 and INV-1003 — and the button reads "Export 3 invoices as CSV" under every one of the six filter states.

focus.title: The new tests landed in a file the spec did not name
focus.detail: The spec listed app/invoices/page.test.tsx as a new file, but that file already exists on main. The builder left it alone and added the nine filter tests as app/invoices/page.filter.test.tsx, which is not in the spec's files list. Nothing is broken by this — both files run and pass, and the two pre-existing tests still render <InvoicesPage /> with no searchParams — but it is a deviation from the declared file list that a reviewer should sign off on rather than discover.

focus.title: /invoices is no longer prerendered
focus.detail: The build output moved /invoices from ○ (Static) to ƒ (Dynamic). The spec predicted this and asked that it not be worked around, and it is not: there is no `export const dynamic` and the query is read on the server, not in the client. Worth knowing if anything downstream assumed that page was static.
